ap_biology-m01.stem: A student isolated four nucleic acid samples and measured the percent of each base in each one. The table shows the results; one sample is RNA, and the others are DNA. The student heats each double-stranded DNA sample slowly. Which sample is predicted to need the highest temperature to separate its two strands?

stimulus.description: Percent of each base in four nucleic acid samples

options.text: Sample X, because it has equal amounts of A and T and equal amounts of G and C.
options.why: All three DNA samples have equal amounts of A and T and of G and C, so this feature does not distinguish them.

options.text: Sample W, because it is double-stranded DNA with the highest percent of G-C pairs, which are held together by three hydrogen bonds.
options.why: Samples with equal A and T and equal G and C are double-stranded DNA; sample Z has unequal amounts and is single-stranded RNA. Among the DNA samples, sample W has 56% G-C, the highest, so it has the most three-hydrogen-bond pairs and needs the highest temperature to separate.

options.text: Sample Z, because it has the highest percent of G and C of all the samples.
options.why: This sample has uracil and unequal amounts of A and U and of G and C, so it is single-stranded RNA and has no second strand to separate.

options.text: Sample Y, because it has the highest percent of A-T pairs, which are held together by the most hydrogen bonds.
options.why: A-T pairs have two hydrogen bonds, fewer than the three of G-C pairs, so a sample rich in A-T pairs separates at a lower temperature.

blueprint.concept: identify double-stranded DNA from base percents and predict strand separation from G-C content
student_thinking: Use equal A and T and equal G and C to identify the double-stranded DNA samples
Calculate the percent of G-C pairs for each DNA sample
Relate more three-hydrogen-bond pairs to a higher separation temperature

key_conditions.condition: every quantity or fact needed is given in the stem or the stimulus

misconceptions.description: All three DNA samples have equal amounts of A and T and of G and C, so this feature does not distinguish them.
This sample has uracil and unequal amounts of A and U and of G and C, so it is single-stranded RNA and has no second strand to separate.
A-T pairs have two hydrogen bonds, fewer than the three of G-C pairs, so a sample rich in A-T pairs separates at a lower temperature.

verification.independent_path: Chargaff equalities per sample then maximum G+C among double-stranded samples vs the generating GC percents

blueprint.judgment_demand: classify the samples before using G-C content to predict

ap_biology-m02.stem: A spherical cell with a radius of 6 µm takes up a nutrient across its surface at a rate of 1.08 nmol per µm² per hour, and uses the nutrient at a rate of 0.3 nmol per µm³ per hour. The cell then grows until its radius is twice as large, without changing its shape or rates. Which prediction about the ability of the cell to meet its demand for the nutrient is best supported?

options.text: No; after the radius doubles, the uptake could supply only 45% of the demand, because the surface area increases two-fold and the volume eight-fold.
options.why: The surface area of a sphere increases with the square of the radius, so doubling the radius increases the surface area four-fold and not two-fold.

options.text: Yes; after the radius doubles, the uptake could still supply 360% of the demand, because the surface area increases four-fold and the volume only two-fold.
options.why: The volume of a sphere increases with the cube of the radius, so doubling the radius increases the volume eight-fold and not two-fold.

options.text: No; after the radius doubles, the uptake could supply only 90% of the demand, because the volume increases eight-fold and the surface area only four-fold.
options.why: At a radius of 6 µm the uptake supplies 180% of the demand (3j/(kr) = 3(1.08)/(0.3 x 6) = 1.8). When the radius doubles, the ratio halves to 0.9, so only 90% of the demand can be met.

options.text: Yes; after the radius doubles, the uptake could still supply 180% of the demand, because the ratio does not depend on the size of the cell.
options.why: The surface area to volume ratio decreases as the radius increases, so the fraction of demand that uptake can supply decreases.

ap_biology-m03.stem: Pieces of beet tissue were placed in water at different temperatures, and the absorbance of the red pigment that leaked into the water was measured. A water blank and a sample of boiled tissue, in which all the pigment was released, were also measured. The table shows the absorbance of each sample. Which statement correctly describes the leakage of the pigment as a percent of the total pigment?

stimulus.description: Absorbance of the solution around beet tissue after 10 minutes at different temperatures

options.text: The pigment leakage increased from 8% at 35 °C to 55% at 55 °C of the total pigment.
options.why: The percent leakage is (absorbance - blank)/(boiled - blank) x 100. At 35 °C it is (0.112 - 0.050)/(0.820 - 0.050) = 8%, and at 55 °C it is (0.473 - 0.050)/(0.820 - 0.050) = 55%.

options.text: The pigment leakage increased from 14% at 35 °C to 58% at 55 °C of the total pigment.
options.why: This does not subtract the absorbance of the water blank from the readings before comparing them with the boiled sample.

options.text: The pigment leakage increased from 0.06% at 35 °C to 0.42% at 55 °C of the total pigment.
options.why: The corrected absorbance is not a percent; it must be divided by the corrected absorbance of the boiled sample and multiplied by 100.

options.text: The pigment leakage increased from 55% at 35 °C to 8% at 55 °C of the total pigment.
options.why: The values are reversed: leakage is lower at the lower temperature.

blueprint.subject: ap_biology
blueprint.concept: describe pigment leakage as a percent of the total after correcting for a blank
student_thinking: Subtract the absorbance of the water blank from each reading
Divide each corrected reading by the corrected absorbance of the boiled tissue
Convert to percent and describe the change between the two temperatures

key_conditions.condition: every quantity or fact needed is given in the stem or the stimulus

misconceptions.description: This does not subtract the absorbance of the water blank from the readings before comparing them with the boiled sample.
The corrected absorbance is not a percent; it must be divided by the corrected absorbance of the boiled sample and multiplied by 100.
The values are reversed: leakage is lower at the lower temperature.

verification.independent_path: corrected ratios vs the generating leakage fractions

blueprint.judgment_demand: correct for the blank and for the total before describing the change

ap_biology-m04.stem: Four dialysis bags with different starting masses and different sucrose concentrations were placed in beakers of distilled water for 30 minutes. The table shows the mass of each bag before and after. Which statement correctly describes the changes in mass?

stimulus.description: Mass of dialysis bags before and after 30 minutes in water

options.text: Bag A had the greatest percent increase in mass, 12%.
options.why: Bag A lost mass, so its change is a decrease and not an increase.

options.text: Bag B had the greatest percent increase in mass, 16%.
options.why: Bag B gained the most mass in grams (3.2 g), but its percent increase is not the greatest.

options.text: Bag D had the greatest percent increase in mass, 24%.
options.why: Percent change = (final - starting)/starting x 100. bag A: -12%; bag B: 16%; bag C: 4%; bag D: 24%. The greatest percent increase is for bag D.

options.text: Bag D had the greatest percent increase in mass, 2.4%.
options.why: The number is the change in mass in grams, not the percent of the starting mass.

blueprint.subject: ap_biology
blueprint.concept: describe mass changes of dialysis bags as percent change
student_thinking: Calculate the change in mass of each bag
Divide each change by the starting mass of the same bag to find the percent change
Compare the percent changes and report the largest increase

key_conditions.condition: every quantity or fact needed is given in the stem or the stimulus

misconceptions.description: Bag A lost mass, so its change is a decrease and not an increase.

verification.independent_path: final/initial ratios vs the generating percent changes

ap_biology-m05.stem: A red blood cell has a solute concentration equivalent to 300 mOsm and is at its normal volume in an isotonic solution. The cell is placed in a solution with an osmolarity of 240 mOsm. Assume that only water can cross the plasma membrane, that the amount of solute in the cell does not change, and that the cell bursts if its volume becomes more than 1.5 times its normal volume. Which prediction is best supported?

options.text: The cell would swell to 1.25 times its original volume and not burst.
options.why: The amount of solute stays constant, so the volume changes in inverse proportion to the osmolarity of the cell's contents: V = 300/240 = 1.25 times the normal volume. This is less than 1.5, so the cell does not burst.

options.text: The cell would swell to 0.25 times its original volume and not burst.
options.why: The final volume is the ratio of the cell osmolarity to the solution osmolarity, which is a multiple of the original volume and not an increase of that amount.

options.text: The cell would swell to 1.25 times its original volume and burst.
options.why: A red blood cell bursts when its volume exceeds 1.5 times the original volume; 1.25 is below this value.

options.text: The cell would shrink to 0.80 times its original volume, because water would move out of the cell.
options.why: The solution has a lower solute concentration than the cell, so water moves into the cell, and the cell swells.

blueprint.subject: ap_biology
blueprint.concept: predict cell volume change from tonicity and a bursting limit
student_thinking: Compare the osmolarity of the solution with the osmolarity of the cell to decide the direction of water movement
Calculate the final volume from the conserved amount of solute
Compare the final volume with the volume at which the cell bursts

key_conditions.condition: every quantity or fact needed is given in the stem or the stimulus

misconceptions.description: The final volume is the ratio of the cell osmolarity to the solution osmolarity, which is a multiple of the original volume and not an increase of that amount.
A red blood cell bursts when its volume exceeds 1.5 times the original volume; 1.25 is below this value.
The solution has a lower solute concentration than the cell, so water moves into the cell, and the cell swells.

verification.independent_path: solute-conservation volume calculation vs ratio of osmolarities

blueprint.judgment_demand: combine tonicity with a quantitative limit to predict the outcome

ap_biology-m05.stem: A red blood cell has a solute concentration equivalent to 300 mOsm and is at its normal volume in an isotonic solution. The cell is placed in a solution with an osmolarity of 120 mOsm. Assume that only water can cross the plasma membrane, that the amount of solute in the cell does not change, and that the cell bursts if its volume becomes more than 1.5 times its normal volume. Which prediction is best supported?

options.text: The cell would shrink to 0.40 times its original volume, because water would move out of the cell.
options.why: The solution has a lower solute concentration than the cell, so water moves into the cell, and the cell swells.

options.text: The cell would swell to 2.50 times its original volume and not burst.
options.why: A red blood cell bursts when its volume exceeds 1.5 times the original volume; 2.50 is above this value.

options.text: The cell would swell to 1.50 times its original volume and not burst.
options.why: The final volume is the ratio of the cell osmolarity to the solution osmolarity, which is a multiple of the original volume and not an increase of that amount.

options.text: The cell would swell to 2.50 times its original volume and burst.
options.why: The amount of solute stays constant, so the volume changes in inverse proportion to the osmolarity of the cell's contents: V = 300/120 = 2.50 times the normal volume. This is more than 1.5, so the cell bursts.

ap_biology-m06.stem: A student counted 500 cells in root tips from a control group and from a group treated with a drug, and recorded the stage of each cell. The table shows the counts. The cell cycle of these cells takes 24 hours in both groups, and the time spent in a stage is proportional to the fraction of cells in that stage. Which claim is best supported by the data?

stimulus.description: Number of cells in each stage among 500 cells counted in each group of root tips

options.text: The drug increased the time that a cell spends in metaphase from about 576 minutes to about 2304 minutes, which suggests that it interferes with the progress of cells out of metaphase.
options.why: These times are ten times too large; a stage occupying a small fraction of the cells uses only that fraction of the cell cycle time.

options.text: The drug decreased the time that a cell spends in anaphase from about 29 minutes to about 14 minutes, which suggests that it speeds up cell division.
options.why: Anaphase is shorter because fewer cells reach it from the blocked metaphase, which does not mean that the cycle is faster; the largest change is the accumulation of cells in metaphase.

options.text: The drug increased the number of cells in metaphase from 20 to 80 but did not change the time that a cell spends in metaphase.
options.why: A larger fraction of cells in a stage means that cells spend more time in that stage, if the total cycle length is unchanged.

options.text: The drug increased the time that a cell spends in metaphase from about 58 minutes to about 230 minutes, which suggests that it interferes with the progress of cells out of metaphase.
options.why: Time in metaphase = fraction x 1440 min. The control has 20/500 x 1440 = 58 min, and the drug-treated group has 80/500 x 1440 = 230 min.

ap_biology-m07.stem: In a culture of 4,000 cells, 10% of the cells have damaged DNA. In cells with a functioning p53 protein, the G1 checkpoint stops 90% of the cells with damaged DNA from entering S phase. In a culture of the same cells that have a mutated p53 gene, the checkpoint stops only 30% of the cells with damaged DNA. How many cells with damaged DNA are predicted to enter S phase in the culture with the mutated p53 gene?

options.why: Leaves out the percent of cells with damaged DNA and applies the checkpoint to all cells in the culture.
Uses the percent of damaged cells that are stopped by the mutant checkpoint instead of the percent that continue.
There are 4,000 x 10% = 400 cells with damaged DNA. 70% of them pass the weakened checkpoint, so 400 x 0.7 = 280 cells enter S phase.
Gives the number of damaged cells in the culture before the checkpoint acts.

ap_biology-m08.stem: A researcher measured the DNA content of 500 cells in a control culture and 500 cells in a culture treated with a drug. The table shows the number of cells with each amount of DNA, where C is the amount of DNA in a haploid cell. Which statement correctly describes the change in the percent of cells in each group?

stimulus.description: Number of cells with each amount of DNA among 500 cells measured in each group

options.text: The percent of cells with 2C of DNA increased from 50% to 65%, and the percent of cells with 4C of DNA decreased from 32% to 17%.
options.why: This reverses the control and treated groups.

options.text: The number of cells with 4C of DNA increased from 85 to 160, so the percent of cells with 4C of DNA doubled.
options.why: The counts must be divided by the total number of cells before percents are compared, and the percent did not necessarily double.

options.text: The percent of cells with 4C of DNA increased from 17% to 32%, and the percent of cells with 2C of DNA decreased from 65% to 50%.
options.why: Percent = number/500 x 100. The control has 65% at 2C, 18% in S, and 17% at 4C. The treated group has 50%, 18%, and 32%.

options.text: The percent of cells with between 2C and 4C of DNA changed from 18% to 33%, which is the largest change.
options.why: The percent of cells in S phase did not change; the largest changes are in the cells with 2C and 4C of DNA.

ap_biology-m09.stem: A testcross was used to measure the recombination frequency between each pair of three linked genes. The table shows the results, and one map unit corresponds to a recombination frequency of 1%. Assume that no double crossovers occurred. Which statement correctly gives the order of the genes and the support for it?

stimulus.description: Recombination frequency between pairs of three genes in a testcross

options.text: The order is B-A-C, because the largest recombination frequency is between B and C, and the distance between B and C is 30 map units.
options.why: The pair with the largest recombination frequency (B and C, 30%) is at the two ends, so A is in the middle. The distance B-A (10) plus A-C (20) equals 30 map units.

options.text: The order is B-A-C, because the largest recombination frequency is between B and C, and the distance between B and C is 10 map units.
options.why: The distance between the outer genes is the sum of the two shorter distances and not their difference.

options.text: The order is B-C-A, because the recombination frequency between B and C is larger than between B and A.
options.why: The largest recombination frequency is between B and C, which places them at the two ends and A between them.

options.text: The order is A-B-C, because the smallest recombination frequency is between B and A, and the distance between A and C is 20 map units.
options.why: The two genes with the largest recombination frequency (B and C) are the outer genes, so A is in the middle and not B.
